thread:
sre-bot: [AUTOPAGE] PagerDuty P1 fired for inference-gateway-prod-eu-west1 — HTTP 5xx rate spike. 5m error rate: ~18%, requests returning 502/503. Triggered by alertchain at 23:46 UTC. PD link: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-12345 :rotating_light:

oncall_tier1: @sre-bot acked. I'm on call — starting quick triage checks. Pinging others. :eyes:

marcus: looking at kvcache metrics — large eviction burst around 23:30 coincident with a canary rollout. Also seeing increased tail latency on streaming endpoints. Possible root causes: kv eviction -> cache miss storm -> backend overload.

leo: digging into node metrics — a few gateway pods showing OOM/killed containers and repeated restarts. Not all hosts though. Could be a config regression in the canary.

katie: customer impact? Any spikes in reported errors from support?

incident-bot: Notifying success-team. 12 customer reports opened in the last 10m referencing 502s on /v1/generate and streaming sessions.

oncall_tier1: Good. I'm going to open short mitigations: 1) rollback canary, 2) warm prefix cache, 3) scale out gateway pool, 4) set fallback routing to smaller model to reduce token churn. Executing now.

marcus: rolling back canary — running:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/inference-gateway --to-revision=42
```

leo: initiating drain on gw-canary-3 to push traffic away from suspected host.

ops-bot: Autoscaling request issued: +3 gateway pods in eu-west1 (policy: emergency-burst). Estimated spin-up: ~45-75s.

oncall_tier1: Warming KV prefix cache via the maintenance API (short lived job) to reduce cold misses. Command:
```
redwoodctl cache warm --service=inference-gateway --scope=prefix --top=200
```

katie: Temporarily flipping route priority to fallback model to shed load:
```
redwoodctl route set-priority inference-gateway --model=redwood-v1-small --priority=100 --note="emergency fallback"
```

marcus: rollback completed: rollout undo returned success. New pods are coming up on stable revision. Initial logs show fewer OOMs but still seeing 502s from a subset of upstream hosts.

leo: Found nginx upstream keepalive exhaustion on host gw-12 (connections hitting limits). Quick fix: reload nginx on that host after bumping keepalives. Patch command being applied to the node: `sudo pkill -HUP nginx` (we'll patch via kubectl exec for ephemeral host).

oncall_tier1: PD update: acknowledged by respondent, customers notified via success-team message 23:58 UTC with mitigations in flight.

katie: Cache warm finished; prefix hit-rate improving. Error rate dropping: now ~6% over 3m. Latency for streaming is coming down.

marcus: After nginx reload and additional pods up, 5xxs are mostly resolved for edge hosts. Continuing to monitor for 15m window.

sre-bot: AUTOPAGE update: error rate down to ~3% over 2m. No new customer reports in last 8m. Will auto-close pager if stable for 15m.

oncall_tier1: Leaving notes for postmortem: collect traces for 23:20-00:10 UTC, include canary deployment diff (config + qconfig), kvcache eviction timeline, nginx keepalive metrics, autoscale events. I'll create an incident doc and assign follow-ups.

katie: thumbs up — add a follow-up item to consider circuit-breaker for kv-miss storm and safer canary ramp (smaller step + ramp delay).

marcus: +1. I'll pin the canary config and prepare a rollback playbook snippet.

sre-bot: Closing note: incident transitioning to mitigation -> monitoring. If error rate rises above 5% again, PD will re-open. :white_check_mark:
